messages:
Olivia (PM): Heads-up — we have three incoming support/sales asks that look like duplicates of the 'customer-friendly merge flow' request. Thinking we should treat them as one canonical backlog item and call out owners + a customer-facing status update. Any objections?

Samir (Eng): sounds right. Can we define a quick scoring rubric so we pick the canonical request deterministically? e.g., impact, frequency, estimated effort, revenue signal, SLA risk — 1-5 each.

Jess (Product Ops): +1 to a rubric. Also recommend adding a `merge_candidate` tag on each intake so we can find them with a saved filter. I can add the tag after we pick canonical.

Maria (Support): FYI the three tickets: https://support.example.com/t/3487 (Acme Corp), https://support.example.com/t/3512 (BetaHealth), https://support.example.com/t/3524 (internal pilot). Acme flagged this as "blocking rollout". We need a comms line for Acme ASAP.

TriageBot: Created fallback issue #RID-720 in product backlog for duplicate-requests review (link: https://redwood/issues/720)

Olivia (PM): Proposed merge-score-grid (quick snapshot):
```
ID  | Requestor   | Impact | Freq | Effort | Revenue | SLA | Total
3487| Acme Corp   | 5      | 4    | 3      | 5       | 4   | 21
3512| BetaHealth  | 3      | 2    | 2      | 2       | 2   | 11
3524| Internal    | 2      | 1    | 1      | 1       | 1   | 6

Rules: higher total = canonical. Tie-breaker = revenue then SLA severity.
```
So canonical = 3487 (Acme). Next steps: Samir to own consolidated backlog item, Jess to draft the customer message, Maria to verify wording for Acme.

Samir (Eng): I can own the consolidated item. I'll create a single backlog ticket that includes links to the three support tickets, the score grid above, and acceptance criteria. Need product sign-off on scope: is this "small UX surface change" OR "platform routing + API change"? That affects effort estimate.

Jess (Product Ops): Based on quick read, scope is "small UX + route config" (small) but if we need data model changes then it's larger. I'll draft but mark scope as 'TBD' and include both estimates. Draft response template below — feel free to iterate:
```
Hi <CustomerName>,
Thanks for flagging this. We reviewed related requests and consolidated them into a single backlog item (RID-720). Status: queued for prioritization. Estimated timeframe: Q2 planning window.
If this is blocking a production rollout, please reply with: 1) urgency, 2) expected launch date, 3) any compliance constraints.
Best,
Olivia & Product
```

Maria (Support): That template is good but Acme needs "ETA with risk" included. Also request we mark Acme as P1 contact — they're enterprise and procurement is waiting. Can we move ETA earlier if we drop nonessential scope?

Olivia (PM): Good catch. I'll add an "ETA (best/worst) + scope tradeoffs" line. Tentative ETA if minimal scope: 3 weeks; full scope: 8-10 weeks. I'll escalate to sales if we need to accelerate.

Samir (Eng): Creating consolidated ticket now and adding tags: `merge_candidate`, `customer-facing`, `acme-p1`. Will include the score grid and both technical paths (quick patch vs full). Link will be posted when created.

TriageBot: New issue created: https://redwood/issues/738 (RID-738 consolidated-merge-requests)

Samir (Eng): RID-738 includes: links to support tickets, score grid, proposed acceptance criteria (canonical request covers unified intake, duplicate tagging, and customer status API). Assigning to Olivia for final acceptance and to me for implementation lead.

Maria (Support): Thanks — please ping me when PR is ready so I can update Acme directly. I also added Acme rep contact email in the issue.

Olivia (PM): Will do. For comms, Jess — can you prepare a short private note for Acme acknowledging consolidation and the ETA (best/worst) + tradeoffs? We'll keep BetaHealth and internal pilot looped in.

Jess (Product Ops): On it, will DM draft within 2 hours and drop into RID-738.

Maria (Support): Appreciated, team. :thumbsup:

Olivia (PM): Closing loop here — thanks all. If anything changes I’ll update RID-738 and post an update in #support.
